key_insight: A structured LLM workflow can automatically build, validate, and tune a multi-variable control strategy from a dynamic process model, producing an executable controller design pipeline.
engineering_relevance: This could reduce the manual effort needed to develop decentralized control structures and tuning environments for nonlinear process plants.
method: Break the design into constrained code-generation steps: plant interface, normalization, MV-CV pairing, controller spec, simulation, scenario generation, and evaluation.
Execute and validate each artifact before moving to the next step; repair failed outputs using validation feedback.
Use Bayesian optimization to tune controller parameters against a closed-loop objective combining tracking and disturbance-rejection errors.
evidence_signal: On a nonlinear gas-preheater benchmark, Bayesian optimization improved the closed-loop objective by about 26.5% relative to the workflow-generated initial controller, mainly by improving pressure-loop transients.
watch_item: The results are shown on a single benchmark, so broader validation on larger plantwide control problems is still needed.
paper_title: An LLM-Driven Workflow for Automated Process Control Strategy Generation and Tuning from Dynamic Process Models
